R0038.title: QR Code Login Fraud
R0038.definition: Exploiting the mechanism of mobile app QR code scanning to authorize web login, enabling fraudulent login.
R0038.description: Business mobile apps often support external QR code scanning for app launch and auto-login for convenience and promotion purposes. An attacker only needs to copy the QR code from the business web login page and send it to a victim. Once the victim scans the QR code, the attacker gains web-side account access for the victim.
R0038.influence: The user's account is logged into by the attacker.

references.title: Mass QQ Accounts Stolen: QR Code Login Hijacked and Recorded by Black Market Groups

observables: The same login QR code is scanned and authorized by multiple different devices or geographic regions within a short window after generation
The session IP and device after scan-based authorization deviate significantly from the account's historical usual location and device
The login QR code is not consumed on its original page but completes authorization in another session
A single account repeatedly shows a short-cycle session pattern of scan-login, abnormal operation, then logout
Scan-based authorizations for multiple different accounts within a short window originate from the same device fingerprint or IP range
